text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today, recovering some ground after a brutal week that saw the stock drop nearly 7%. The bounce came as oil prices stabilized—US crude holding around $103 per barrel—and on the heels of a leadership change and company update announced on October 29th. Refineries are running at 92.8% capacity, and fuel inventories remain relatively tight, which supports margins for refiners when crude and finished fuel supplies are constrained.

The broader context matters: the refining sector has been volatile as political pressure mounts on Big Oil over fuel prices, even as actual refining profits have surged due to tight supply conditions. The potential restart of U.S.-Iran negotiations (reported October 31st) could ease geopolitical risk and oil supply concerns that have kept prices elevated, though any deal remains uncertain. For a refiner, lower crude prices would normally help, but tight fuel supplies and refinery utilization near 93% are the real drivers of profitability right now.
